latin.context: Neenga veetukku varappo unga paatti thatha oru virunthaalikitta pesitu irukanga. Unga thatha ithu Saraswathi, unga paattioda thangachinu arimuga paduthuraanga.
latin.question: Neenga tamizhla epdi avungala mariyaathaya koopduvinga

tamil.context: நீங்கள் வீட்டுக்கு வரப்போ உங்க பாட்டி தாத்தா ஒரு விருந்தாளிக்கிட்ட பேசிட்டு இருக்காங்க. உங்க தாத்தா இது சரஸ்வதி, உங்கள் பாட்டியோட தங்கச்சின்னு அறிமுகப்படுத்துறாங்க.
tamil.question: நீங்க தமிழில் எப்படி அவங்களை மரியாதையா கூப்பிடுவீங்க?

english.context: You come home and see see a guest talking to your grandparents. Your grandparents introduce her as Saraswathi, your grandmother's sister.
english.question: How should you address her politely in Tamil?

items.explanation: In Tamil social norms, addressing a guest who is your grandmother's sister as ‘Paatti’ signals respect and appropriate relational distance.

latin.context: Unga teacherah unga kalyanathukku invite panna avunga veetuku poittu, kelamba poringa.
latin.question: Porathukku munnadi enna pannuvinga?

tamil.context: உங்க டீச்சர உங்க கல்யாணத்துக்கு இன்வைட் பண்ண அவங்க வீட்டுக்கு போயிட்டு, கிளம்பப் போறிங்க.
tamil.question: போறதுக்கு முன்னாடி என்ன பண்ணுவீங்க?

english.context: You have invited your teacher to your wedding, and after visiting their home, you are about to leave.
english.question: What will you do before leaving?

answer.label: A
answer.text: Touching his feet as a sign of respect

items.explanation: In Tamil culture, it is customary to show respect to elders and teachers by touching their feet and seeking blessings before departing, especially on significant occasions like weddings.

dialogue.speaker: Sumathi
dialogue.utterance: Kaaikari veetla perusa ethuvum illa, ippo kadaikku poi edhaachu vaangitu varingala

latin.question: Paari "Aproma paathukalam" nu sonna artham enna?

dialogue.speaker: Sumathi
dialogue.utterance: காய்கறி வீட்ட்ல பெருசா எதுவும் இல்லை, இப்போ கடைக்கு போய் எதாச்சு வாங்கிட்டு வரிங்கலா?

tamil.question: பாரி "அப்போமா பாதுக்கலாம்" என்று சொன்னா அர்த்தம் என்ன?

dialogue.speaker: Sumathi
dialogue.utterance: There isn't much in the vegetable house, can you go to the shop and buy something now?

dialogue.speaker: Paari
dialogue.utterance: We can see later, I have work

english.question: What does Paari mean by saying "We can see later"?
options: Go to the shop and see
We can go after some time

items.explanation: Here, Paari uses a polite indirect refusal by saying "We can see later," which implies that he does not want to go to the shop now due to having work. This is a common face-saving strategy in Tamil culture to avoid direct refusals within family contexts.

latin.context: Officela unga cabin la vela paathuttu irukkappo, manager unga kitta pesanumnu varananga.
latin.question: Neenga enna panna koodathu?
options: Manager ninnu pesittu irukkapo neenga ukkanthutu mariyaathai illama pesalam

answer.label: D
answer.text: Manager ninnu pesittu irukkapo neenga ukkanthutu mariyaathai illama pesalam

tamil.context: ஆபீஸ்ல உங்க கேபின்ல வேலை பார்த்துட்டு இருக்கப்போ, மேனேஜர் உங்க கிட்ட பேசணும்னு வராங்க.
tamil.question: நீங்க என்ன பண்ண கூடாது?
options: மேனேஜர் நின்று பேசிட்டு இருக்கப்போ நீங்க உக்கந்துட்டு மரியாதை இல்லாம பேசலாம்

answer.label: D
answer.text: மேனேஜர் நின்று பேசிட்டு இருக்கப்போ நீங்க உக்கந்துட்டு மரியாதை இல்லாம பேசலாம்

english.context: At work, when you are working in your cabin, the manager comes to talk to you.
english.question: What should you not do?
options: Ask him to sit and then talk
When the manager is standing and talking to you, you can sit down and talk without showing respect

answer.label: D
answer.text: When the manager is standing and talking to you, you can sit down and talk without showing respect

items.explanation: In Tamil workplace culture, it is expected to show respect to superiors by standing when they approach and talk to you. Sitting down while the manager is standing can be seen as disrespectful, so the correct answer is that you should not sit down and talk without showing respect.

cultural_markers: expectation to stand when talking to superiors

dialogue.speaker: Vaanathi
dialogue.utterance: Ungala paathu pesunathu manasukku romba niraivaa irukku, odamaba paathukkonga, na varen

dialogue.speaker: Sudhan
dialogue.utterance: Iru iru, na vaasal varaikkum varen

dialogue.speaker: வானதி
dialogue.utterance: உங்களை பார்த்து பேசுனது மனசுக்கு ரொம்ப நிறைவா இருக்கு, ஓடமா பாதுக்கொங்க, நான் வரேன்

dialogue.speaker: சுதன்
dialogue.utterance: இரு இரு, நான் வாசல் வரைக்கும் வரேன்

dialogue.speaker: Vaanathi
dialogue.utterance: It was fulfilling talking to you, take care of your health, I will come back

dialogue.speaker: Sudhan
dialogue.utterance: Wait wait, I will come till the gate

english.question: Why does Sudhan want to go to the gate?
options: Because Vaanathi said she will come back
He is asking Vaanathi not to go

items.explanation: In this dialogue, Sudhan says he will come to the gate to see Vaanathi off. In Tamil social practice, accompanying someone to the gate is a common and respectful way to send them off.

cultural_markers: seeing someone off to the gate

dialogue.speaker: Arun
dialogue.utterance: Aarthi, enga irukka, inga ellarum vandhutaanga, unakkaaga dhan kaathuttu irukkom

dialogue.speaker: Aarthi
dialogue.utterance: Ayo sorry, kelamba neram aayiduchu, neenga aarambinga, na vandhuruven

dialogue.speaker: அருண்
dialogue.utterance: ஆர்த்தி, எங்க இருக்க, இங்க எல்லாரும் வந்துட்டாங்க, உனக்காக தான் காத்துட்டிருக்கோம்

dialogue.speaker: ஆர்த்தி
dialogue.utterance: அய்யோ சோரி, கிளம்ப நேரம் ஆயிடுச்சு, நீங்க ஆரம்பிங்க, நான் வந்துருவேன்

dialogue.speaker: Arun
dialogue.utterance: Aarthi, we are here, everyone has come, we are waiting for you

dialogue.speaker: Aarthi
dialogue.utterance: Oh sorry, it took time to leave, you all start, I will be there

english.question: What should Arun do?
options: Tell Aarthi to leave and start without her

items.explanation: In this dialogue, Arun is waiting for Aarthi to arrive before starting the event. Aarthi apologizes for being late and says that they can start without her. However, in Tamil social norms, it is polite to wait for the person who is late, especially if they are an important part of the event, rather than starting without them.

cultural_markers: Tamil norms of waiting for latecomers
